intro.text: You are two bad decisions away from a felony and one good plan away from winning. Which way are we going?
intro.speaker: Mere

choices.text: What if I already made the bad decisions?

winning.text: Good. Let me see the plan. I'll tell you which parts will get you arrested, which parts will get you killed, and which parts are actually clever. Usually it's a Venn diagram with significant overlap.
winning.speaker: Mere

choices.text: I'll come back with a plan

mere_review.text: Hmm. The rooftop entry? Illegal, but creative. The fake delivery? Illegal, but effective. The part where you disguise yourself as a health inspector? That's actually legal, surprisingly. I checked. You're just missing one thing: an exit strategy that doesn't involve parkour.
mere_review.speaker: Mere

mere_parkour.text: Of course it is. And when you break your ankle — not if, when — remember that I told you so. In writing. I have a draft liability waiver ready. Sign it. It's for my peace of mind.
mere_parkour.speaker: Mere

mere_suggestion.text: Louis has a delivery van. It's registered to a shell company I set up last month. The company name is 'Totally Legitimate Deliveries LLC.' I'm not good at names, I'm good at paperwork. Use the van.
mere_suggestion.speaker: Mere

legal_advice.text: I read contracts so you don't have to. What's the situation? And before you answer, remember that attorney-client privilege only applies if I'm actually your attorney. Which, legally speaking, I'm not. I'm your friend who happens to know a lot about law. Big difference.
legal_advice.speaker: Mere

choices.text: Any legal way to do this?

mere_seen.text: If you got seen, we have options. Option A: It didn't happen. Option B: It happened, but it wasn't you. Option C: It was you, but you were sleepwalking and have no memory. I like Option A. It's clean. Option C requires a doctor's note, and Jake would actually write one, which says worrying things about both of you.
mere_seen.speaker: Mere

mere_legal_way.text: The legal way is to not do it. But since that's apparently off the table, the 'less illegal' way involves permits, licenses, and a shocking amount of paperwork. I can forge — I mean, 'prepare' — all of it. Give me 48 hours.
mere_legal_way.speaker: Mere

mere_48_hours.text: I'm a professional. I can do it in 24 if you don't care about the details being believable. 48 if you want the IRS to nod approvingly. Your call.
mere_48_hours.speaker: Mere

bad_decisions.text: Then we mitigate. That's lawyer-speak for 'make it someone else's problem.' Who saw you? What did they see? Do they have cameras? Do they have lawyers? Most importantly: do they have better lawyers than me? Because if they do, we might need to get creative.
bad_decisions.speaker: Mere

choices.text: No one saw me. I think.

mere_think.text: 'I think' is not a legal defense. 'I know' is barely a legal defense. But it's a start. Next time, know. Or better yet, don't be there to be seen.
mere_think.speaker: Mere

mere_guard.text: A guard. Okay. Guards have bosses. Bosses have insurance. Insurance companies have lawyers. Those lawyers are... adequate. I can work with adequate. The question is: does the guard know he saw you? Or does he think he saw a very athletic raccoon?
mere_guard.speaker: Mere

mere_black.text: Black. At night. Groundbreaking. Next time try a high-visibility vest and a clipboard. No one questions someone with a clipboard. I have seventeen. They're my most effective legal tool.
mere_black.speaker: Mere

goodbye.text: Remember: the law is a tool. Use it before it uses you.
goodbye.speaker: Mere
